limitations: Concept-only review; no native grid, scaled collision, accessible route, engineering, hydraulic, clinical or runtime validation.
No characters or children appear in any of these eight review images; empty furniture does not establish vacancy, death, departure, refusal or consent.
Props do not establish potability, actual inventory, completed payment, staffed care, information-sharing authority or actual delivery.

findings.finding: Consultation care tray and optional blank wall invitation are separate. Linen screen divides desk and examination couch while leaving the exit route beside it; it is a partial visual privacy cue, not proof of full sightline/privacy protection from every doorway. Separate resting hut has one bed, reachable-looking key, closed bag and blank proxy-like card; no people or children appear. Both exits reach visible dry road without a research desk or laboratory checkpoint. Visible shallow entry STEPS conflict with the prompt ground-level/no-step intention; revise accessible threshold/ramp and verify width before any layout use. Empty couch and bed do not prove extra capacity, death, departure, consent, ability to lift objects or actual proxy authorization.

Different-color/age detached pipe rings, closed sample bottle and timing marks are distinct. Short capped elevated pipe is visibly separate from lower open stone channel, with no drawn connection; foreground dry path avoids fenced wet margins. Right shelter has finite lidded blue-tagged buckets, a filled shift-tally tray, separate empty replacement tray and empty stool. Additional barrels are decoration unless actual inventory assigns them. View drifts to diagonal/isometric huts and paving, so retain as material/prop review only, not square-grid layout template. Blue tags, closed lids and water color cannot establish potability, actual supply, causation, stopped contamination or recovery. Empty replacement seat never means a replacement arrived, nor that a resting caregiver abandoned a patient.

Closed ground sample port, capped stub, fixed measuring rod, reference bottle and timing token are visible on dry land; no deep shaft, patient trial or new crystal appears. Waiting space has two separate token trays, cup, bench, empty stool and ladder secured upright to wall rather than lying down. Front and lateral open edges suggest access to the same dry high path, but TWO distinct room exits are not unambiguously constructed; redraw topology before collision work. Distinct tray color is not enough to encode nursing versus maintenance pay without final icons/state. Static tokens do not prove settled wages, arrived maintenance/replacement staff or renewed consent; surface samples add no second N12 evidence/reward.

Exactly two unequal-size earthenware bowls appear on the allocation table, with sparse cloth/jug shelves, an empty shelf bay and separate closed cupboard. The shortage frame contains rods rather than being empty, so it cannot honestly encode an empty/zero slot without refinement. Waiting room has plain bench, reachable-looking cup of water, closed side-shelf observation book and blank personal token; its open front reaches the dry yard without crossing an observation-signing desk. No people, children, signatures or beds are shown. Cup appearance cannot certify potable water. Empty room does not prove refusal, arrival, transfer or consent; actual finite ordinary care and water remain available independently of research participation, subject to real staffing/supply accounting.

overall: Care and observation separation, personal key and two unequal bowls supported. 115 steps require accessible-route revision; 116 perspective and 117 exact two-exit topology require layout redraft. Water and staffing outcomes remain unproven.
